Definition: from G1722 and the base of G5056; to enjoin:--(give) charge, (give) command(-ments), injoin.
BiblicalUsage: To enjoin, to give charge or command. Jesus gave commandments to His apostles through the Holy Ghost before He was taken up in Acts 1:2, Moses sprinkled the blood and said this is the blood of the testament which God has enjoined unto you in Hebrews 9:20, and the devil quotes the promise that God shall give His angels charge over Jesus in Luke 4:10. Jesus answers the devil's misuse with His own obedience: as the Father gave Me commandment, even so I do, in John 14:31.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe commandments are not suggestions — they come with the authority of the one who gives them, and Jesus obeyed His Father's commandment all the way to the cross. I hold that the angels' charge over me is real, but it is God's command, not the devil's quotation, that I live by.
